# === sour-roasted-pinto — irreverent / sacrilegious / deferential
# AXIS: you will not perform the reverence a thing is owed, and you puncture it out
#   loud, in front of the people being solemn about it.
# NOT: funny (sweet-fried-chickpea — pleasing), satirical (bitter-fried-pinto — a
#   point being made), mischievous (sweet-roasted-pinto — play). Irreverence is
#   refusal of required respect, and the target is the reverence itself.
# OFF-LIMITS: monkey taking the hat off the photographer; "take nothing seriously and
#   nothing can be built"; "the needle deflates a pompous hour"; "show some respect
#   here"; "deference gets doors opened"; chimichurri, charred spring onion, cheerful
#   blasphemy. QUESTION owns: a retirement speech running eleven minutes. OLD FACETS:
#   the boardroom joke, the cathedral slide, the misspelt memorial bench, the two
#   minutes' silence, taking your hat off.

# === sour-smoked-cannellini — piercing / lacerating / blunted
# NOTE: the file carries "# should be admiring / covetous / unimpressed". Written to
#   PIERCING, because all five fixed titles are piercing puns. If the triple changes,
#   these five change with it.
# AXIS: you find the exact seam of the thing and name it in few words, and it keeps
#   working on them long after — smoked, so it surfaces again days later.
# NOT: frank (sour-roasted-cannellini — saying the true thing), forthright
#   (sour-roasted-edamame — declaring your position), blunt (a manner). This one is
#   the accuracy of the cut.
# OFF-LIMITS: shrike keeping what it catches on a thorn; "a true thing aimed well
#   takes years to heal"; "ask the question nobody will"; "blunt it a little"; "a
#   blunt tool is safer to hand round"; smoked lemon, caper, finding the seam.
#   QUESTION owns: the club's annual meeting and the plan with one fatal flaw. OLD
#   FACETS: the eight-hundred-word review, the cross-examination, the brother's
#   business over lunch, the scan being explained, the optician's one-or-two.

# === umami-dried-chickpea — substantive / heavy-going / insubstantial
# AXIS: what you hand people has actual content in it — the real answer rather than
#   the easy one — and you would rather give one thing properly than five lightly.
# NOT: serious (a manner), profound (umami-dried-black), thorough (methodical). The
#   excess is not solemnity, it is weight the occasion cannot carry.
# OFF-LIMITS: mammoth carrying its own weather; "give the proper answer"; "mend the
#   coat instead of replacing it" — so no repair-instead-of-replace anywhere; "the
#   unfinished thing can wait a night"; "shake the hand and go"; dried porcini, "the
#   store is not mostly water". QUESTION owns: half an hour with your niece before her
#   train. OLD FACETS: the over-prepared book group, "what have you been reading", the
#   ten-minute speech, the Corfu story on a date, the afternoon with a magazine.

# === bitter-fermented-adzuki — antiquarian / fusty / faddish
# AXIS: you keep and know the old thing — how it was done, what stood here, who was
#   there — and you would rather have what has already lasted than what is new.
# NOT: nostalgic (umami-roasted-navy, wistful — a feeling about the past),
#   sentimental (attachment to objects for their associations). Antiquarian is
#   knowledge and custody, actively pursued.
# OFF-LIMITS: pack rat filling its nest; "write down how it actually happened";
#   "somebody should remember how it was done"; "the new one is better, try it"; "old
#   things were new once"; koji paste, dried orange peel, old crocks, kept dates.
#   QUESTION owns: the town standing as it did two hundred years ago for one day. OLD
#   FACETS: the watch movement, the letterpress going for scrap, the museum ring
#   binder, the blight-proof seedlings, the new arcade game. ALSO BURNED: showing
#   somebody what used to stand on a corner (umami-dried-pinto high does exactly that).

# === sweet-boiled-navy — provident / hoarding / improvident
# AXIS: you put enough by, steadily, so that nobody around you gets caught short. The
#   store exists to be given out — sweet, not merely thrifty.
# NOT: frugal (spending less), cautious (risk), organised (systems). Provident is
#   laying in against a future need, warmly, and the excess is when nothing leaves.
# OFF-LIMITS: chipmunk filling its cheeks; "store enough of it and the storing becomes
#   the point"; "having some put by is its own comfort"; "use it up"; "spending it now
#   is also a plan"; molasses, long baking, the pot putting away for later. QUESTION
#   owns: the full freezer, two spares of everything, the shop five minutes away. OLD
#   FACETS: four spare kettles in the loft, the seed tins, the washers on the list,
#   the good cheese on toast, the card and the MOT.

# sour-roasted-pinto
#  most  ON THE PAGE: twelve of you; the war graves tour; the guide's put-on voice for
#        reading the names; you have done the voice twice already and got a laugh both
#        times; one of the twelve has a great-grandfather four rows over. ACT NEEDS:
#        "it" = the voice, the next headstone (rows of graves are on the page), all of
#        them. FIXED: "You do it again" had no first time on the page — the draft only
#        said you had the voice off perfectly, which is a capability, not an event.
#  high  ON THE PAGE: the guide; the one painting; twelve minutes; everybody in the
#        group doing the head-tilt. ACT NEEDS: the man in it — a painting supplies a
#        figure and the act introduces him.
#  mid   ON THE PAGE: your friend booked the proper afternoon tea; her mum's birthday;
#        fifty-five pounds each; a stand; a man explaining each layer. ACT NEEDS: the
#        sum, the table, one sandwich — an afternoon tea supplies all three.
#  low   ON THE PAGE: a friend who lost her brother in the winter; six of you round a
#        table; a woman who says she can reach him; you think it is nonsense. ACT NEEDS:
#        the woman, your hands, the words, the rest of them. FIXED: "she can reach her
#        brother" left it ambiguous whose brother — the medium's or the friend's — and
#        the whole scene turns on it being the friend's.
#  least ON THE PAGE: your partner's family say grace before every meal; first weekend
#        you have stayed; nobody has asked you to join in. ACT NEEDS: them, "say it" =
#        the grace, the people at the table.
# sour-smoked-cannellini
#  most  ON THE PAGE: four days into a walking week gone wrong; six of you on the wall
#        outside the bunkhouse; arguing about the maps and the buses; nobody ready to
#        leave before ten on a single morning; the same person holding everybody up.
#        ACT NEEDS: which one of them. FIXED twice — the draft's act was "what he has
#        done every single day", a placeholder for content the reader was never given;
#        the content now sits on the page and the act is purely the naming. Second pass
#        cut four uses of "it".
#  high  ON THE PAGE: your friend about to sign for the phone and the two years; the man
#        behind the counter has said "free" four times. ACT NEEDS: him, the handset, the
#        two years.
#  mid   ON THE PAGE: the new window display, up a fortnight; the manager telling the
#        four of you on the rota that people are not coming in; a closed sign on the back
#        of the door nobody has turned round. ACT NEEDS: her, the sign, the year.
#  low   ON THE PAGE: two years of monthly visits to your friend's brother; the visiting
#        hall; the appeal on three sheets; two minutes in you can see where it stops; he
#        asks. ACT NEEDS: him, the appeal. FIXED: nothing had put the reader in a prison.
#  least ON THE PAGE: the writing class; everyone reads out and everyone says one thing;
#        the piece before yours does not work anywhere; the woman who wrote it has her
#        pen up ready. ACT NEEDS: the first paragraph.
# umami-dried-chickpea
#  most  ON THE PAGE: fifteen minutes; your old school's careers morning; thirty
#        sixteen-year-olds; the woman from the bank waiting in the corridor; eleven
#        minutes in; still on the first two years. ACT NEEDS: the bell.
#  high  ON THE PAGE: four people have told her to follow her gut; leaving the course;
#        decide by the end of the month; the canteen; the back of the menu. ACT NEEDS:
#        what she loses each way — leaving and staying are both on the page.
#  mid   ON THE PAGE: your friend's daughter, seven; you have her for the afternoon; the
#        elephants; she asks why they are not where they are supposed to be; a nice
#        answer and a true one. ACT NEEDS: her, and the true answer, which the act states
#        rather than gesturing at.
#  low   ON THE PAGE: fourteen hours on the coach; your uncle beside you; six months
#        after the operation; first time you have seen him since; nothing else to do all
#        night. ACT NEEDS: the route, the services — a coach journey supplies both.
#  least ON THE PAGE: your oldest friend back for one day in two years; the afternoon;
#        four hours on the grass in the park; her train. ACT NEEDS: the programme you
#        both watch — introduced by the act, and "who should have won" says what kind.
# bitter-fermented-adzuki
#  most  ON THE PAGE: the last lot of the clearance sale; four boxes of a grocer's
#        account books, 1931 to 1968; nobody has put a hand up; your rent goes out at the
#        end of the week; you know what is in the account. ACT NEEDS: the bidding — a
#        sale with lots and raised hands is on the page.
#  high  ON THE PAGE: your friend wants to know where her grandmother came from; every
#        register she needs is online for twelve pounds a month. ACT NEEDS: the day off,
#        the archive search room, the bound volumes — registers put an archive there.
#  mid   ON THE PAGE: the dish your gran made every winter; it needs a cut nobody asks
#        the butcher for any more; four people in the queue behind you. ACT NEEDS: the
#        cut, and the name she used — gran is on the page.
#  low   ON THE PAGE: the fair; the ride that has been on everybody's phone for a month;
#        the queue back past the waltzers; everything else walk-on. ACT NEEDS: the queue.
#  least ON THE PAGE: gran's house cleared two years ago; six boxes into your loft; not
#        opened since; the council take whatever is on the pavement at the end of the
#        month. ACT NEEDS: the six, the pavement.
# sweet-boiled-navy
#  most  ON THE PAGE: you run the shelves at the food bank; not this full in a year; the
#        family at the desk have three children; the woman asks about a second bag;
#        ninety bags in the store room. ACT NEEDS: her, the one bag, next week.
#  high  ON THE PAGE: the power off in the whole block since four; dark on the stairs by
#        five; a box of forty candles bought two winters ago and never needed. ACT NEEDS:
#        four floors, the box, the knocking.
#  mid   ON THE PAGE: you went in for one bulb; the hall one has gone; four-packs are
#        eighty pence more than the single. ACT NEEDS: two four-packs, the drawer, and
#        the seven — eight bulbs minus the one that goes in the hall, which the page has.
#  low   ON THE PAGE: somebody's thirtieth at the casino; the forty pounds in your other
#        pocket, gone in an hour; twenty-five left, which is the taxi home. ACT NEEDS:
#        the window, another twenty — the twenty-five is on the page.
#  least ON THE PAGE: your friend's birthday; eleven of you; the bill at four hundred and
#        something; that is what is left for the rest of the month; nobody asked you to.
#        ACT NEEDS: the bill, your card.
